note: Battles (v2 step 6). A field of three lanes and a reserve. Each side places its companies; over up to `rounds` rounds each lane fights: a side's lane power is the sum of its companies' strength times power, times the terrain and weather for their kind. Each company loses `loss` x the enemy lane's power / its own lane's power (at most `maxLoss`) a round; a lane left empty lets the enemy turn the flank, adding `flank` of that lane's power to the centre. Morale falls with losses (`morale` per point of strength lost, as a share of the side's whole) and breaks below `rout`. Between rounds the reserve can be committed to a lane; a side can sound the retreat (losing `retreatLoss` more). The side with more power and morale left wins. Sieges: walled places have a garrison by kind; a besieged city eats its stores and falls when they run out; it can be stormed (its garrison fights behind walls, `walls` stronger), or offered terms when the besiegers are `termsRatio` times its garrison or its stores are nearly gone.
